metadata.neutral_citation: LEE HON CHEUNG v. CHAN TANG KAI LAN AND ANOTHER [1995] HKCFI 15; [1995] 3 HKC 640; HCA 4522/1991 (30 October 1995)
metadata.case_name: LEE HON CHEUNG v. CHAN TANG KAI LAN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Mr Lee fractured his femoral shaft
source: Mr Lee fractured his femoral shaft and the proximal part of his left tibia.

injuries.description: fracture of the proximal part of his left tibia
source: Mr Lee fractured his femoral shaft and the proximal part of his left tibia.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia, unspecified

injuries.description: very severe head injuries including cerebral oedema and prolonged post-traumatic amnesia
source: In my judgment, in view of the long period of PTA the head injuries could be described as very severe head injuries.
There is a 10% impairment of the whole person in respect of his post-traumatic amnesia, the period of confusion and mental disturbance and headache.

injuries.description: two deep lacerations over the left eyebrow and forehead with resulting scar and deficiency of the eyebrow
injuries.body_part: left forehead / left eyebrow / left lateral side of left eye
source: On admission to the hospital there were two deep lacerations over the left eyebrow and forehead measuring 4 cm and 6 cm respectively.

when Mr Lee was examined by Dr Philip Mao in June 1993 there was a 3¼ inch long vertical oblique scar running from the left forehead and slicing through the left eyebrow at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds with deficiency of the eyebrow. The scar continued downwards to the lateral side of the left eye.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: multiple keloidal irregular scars on the lateral and anterior surfaces of the upper part of the left thigh
source: There are multiple keloidal irregular scars totalling eight in all on the lateral and anterior services of the upper part of the left thigh.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

injuries.description: puncture holes on either side of the heel bone where pins had been inserted
source: On either side of the heel bone there are puncture holes where the pins had been inserted.
injuries.icd_description: Puncture wound without foreign body of ankle or foot

manifestations.description: disorientated and confused for about 3 weeks
withdrawn and showed less concern in his schoolworks; temper now is irritable, easily provoked
mild limping gait with shortening of his left lower limb by about 1.5 cm
a 15o medial angualation in the femoral fracture
some stiffness of his left knee and wasting of the left thigh muscle
limitation of movement and he could not bend his left leg
pain from the scaring tissue and worry about his scars on the face

treatments_received: two operations in the fractured limb (pin insertion)
traction (pin inserted into the heel region) and then long leg dynacast

losses.description: the head injuries had manifested themselves in the cognitive impairment of Mr Lee and in his personality changes; deterioration in school works particularly those involving more abstract or conceptual thinking
withdrawn and showed less concern in his schoolworks; temper now is irritable, easily provoked
He said he suffered pain from the scaring tissue, he was also worried about his scars on the face which was very apparent, he tended to think people would star him because of the scars.
multiple keloidal irregular scars totalling eight in all on the lateral and anterior services of the upper part of the left thigh
mild limping gait with shortening of his left lower limb by about 1.5 cm; limitation of movement and he could not bend his left leg

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: As a result of the leg injuries he was not able to assert as much force with his left leg and he tried to avoid kicking with his left leg.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Dr Kan was of the view that Mr Lee could not possibly have entered tertiary institutes.
